title: Bi-directional relationship without a clear modeling requirement
rationale: Bidirectional filtering can hurt performance and create confusing filter behavior.
evidence_required: Relationship cross-filter direction and model paths
review_note: Valid for specific many-to-many, one-to-one, slicer-with-data or dimension-to-dimension scenarios.

title: Many-to-many relationship without explicit bridge/design rationale
rationale: Uncontrolled many-to-many relationships can create ambiguous or surprising results.
review_note: Many-to-many is valid when deliberately designed.

title: Ambiguous filter propagation path
rationale: Multiple active filter paths can create unpredictable behavior or model ambiguity.
review_note: Some scenarios use inactive relationships intentionally; verify semantics.

title: One-to-one relationship used where tables could be consolidated
rationale: One-to-one relationships are often avoidable and add model complexity.
review_note: May be needed for security, storage mode or source-bound constraints.

title: Inactive relationship exists without a visible usage pattern
rationale: Unused inactive relationships add maintenance complexity.
review_note: May be reserved for future or specialized calculations; verify documentation.

title: Relationship keys have incompatible or inefficient data types
rationale: Relationship key consistency is important for correctness and efficient model behavior.
review_note: Technical surrogate keys may intentionally differ from source business keys.
